answer: Each identity is verified by a Wesolowski time-lock proof built from continuous, sequential modular squarings: each result depends on the previous one, so GPUs cannot parallelize a single chain to shorten its elapsed time. An attacker may run many clone chains concurrently, but each requires its own computation and hardware resources, making Sybil identities costly under a fixed time and compute budget. The anchor, velvet, and opal labels do not change this bottleneck.
